1.title: Transform Columns and Rows
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Transform Columns and Rows. It covers the exam area Prepare the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Select appropriate column data types. Create and transform columns. Group and aggregate rows. Pivot, unpivot, and transpose data. Convert semi-structured data to a table. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Prepare the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Select appropriate column data types
1.text: Select appropriate column data types. A column's data type controls what you can do with it. Set the type in the Power Query Editor with the data type icon in the column header or with Data Type on the Transform tab.

1.title: Select appropriate column data types, continued
1.text: Select appropriate column data types. The figure shows this: Pivot turns the values of one column into new columns with an aggregate, and unpivot turns many columns into attribute and value rows.

1.title: Select appropriate column data types, continued
1.text: Select appropriate column data types. Aggregation. Numbers can be summed and averaged; text cannot. Sorting. Text sorts alphabetically, so "ten" comes before "two". Relationships. The two key columns need the same type. Compression. Numbers and dates compress better than text. Whole Number. Counts and integer keys. Decimal Number. General measurements. Fixed decimal number. Money, with four digits after the decimal point. Date, Time, Date or Time. Calendar values; remove the time part from a date key. Text. Names and codes. True or False. Flags.

1.title: Select appropriate column data types, continued
1.text: Select appropriate column data types. Power Query adds a Changed Type step when it detects types. Check it, because a column left as Any has no type. If dates or numbers come in another culture's format, such as day before month, use Data Type, then Using Locale and pick the culture. Converting without the right locale can produce errors or swapped days and months. Exam tip: Relationship key columns must have the same data type, and a date key should have no time part. Use Using Locale when the source format follows another culture.

1.title: Create and transform columns
1.text: Create and transform columns. New columns come from the Add Column tab. Most transformations are on the Transform tab. Custom Column. You can write an M expression. Column From Examples. You type sample results and Power Query infers the rule. Conditional Column. You need if, else if, else rules without writing code. Index Column. You need a row number, starting at zero, one or a custom value. Split Column. One column holds several parts: split by delimiter, by number of characters or by positions.

1.title: Create and transform columns, continued
1.text: Create and transform columns. Merge Columns. You join columns with a separator into one new column. Extract. You need the length, first or last characters, a range, or text before, after or between delimiters.

1.title: Create and transform columns, continued
1.text: Create and transform columns. Merge Columns replaces the selected columns with the new one. M is case-sensitive: if, then and else must be lowercase and column names must match exactly. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Conditional Column is the no-code choice for if-then rules, Column From Examples infers a rule from samples, and Custom Column needs an M formula. Pick the one the requirement words allow.

1.title: Group and aggregate rows
1.text: Group and aggregate rows. Group By collapses many rows into one row per group. It is on the Home tab and the Transform tab. In the basic dialog you choose one column to group by and one aggregation. The advanced dialog allows several group columns and several aggregations.

1.title: Group and aggregate rows, continued
1.text: Group and aggregate rows. Sum, Average, Median. The total, mean or middle value of a column. Min, Max. The smallest or largest value. Count Rows. The number of rows in each group. Count Distinct Rows. The number of different values in a column. All Rows. A nested table of the group's rows, which you can expand. Group By also reduces granularity: grouping order lines by store and day gives a smaller table, which helps model size (module eight). Remember that grouping loses the detail of the original rows, so keep the detail if reports need it. Exam tip: Group By makes one row per group; All Rows keeps the detail as a nested table. Use Count Rows for row counts and Count Distinct Rows for different values.

1.title: Pivot, unpivot and transpose
1.text: Pivot, unpivot and transpose. These commands change the shape of the table. They are on the Transform tab. Pivot Column. Turns the values of one column into new column headers; you choose a values column and an aggregate function such as Sum, Count or Don't Aggregate. Unpivot Columns. Turns the selected columns into Attribute and Value rows. Unpivot Other Columns. You select the columns to keep; every other column is unpivoted, including columns added to the source later.

1.title: Pivot, unpivot and transpose, continued
1.text: Pivot, unpivot and transpose. Unpivot Only Selected Columns. Unpivots only the named columns; columns added later are not unpivoted. Transpose. Rotates the table: rows become columns and columns become rows.

1.title: Pivot, unpivot and transpose, continued
1.text: Pivot, unpivot and transpose. A report needs tall, tidy data with one row per fact, such as Product, Month and Amount. A sheet with one column per month is wide, so unpivot it. Pivot is the opposite and is used to make a summary layout. Transpose does not keep the headers as headers. Run Use Headers as First Row first if you need the old headers as data, then Transpose, then Use First Row as Headers. Transpose also resets the data types, so set them again. Exam tip: When new columns will keep arriving, use Unpivot Other Columns and select only the columns to keep. Pivot Column needs an aggregate function, and Transpose needs Use First Row as Headers afterward.

2.title: Convert semi-structured data to a table
2.text: Convert semi-structured data to a table. Jason and X M L hold nested data. Connect with the Jason or X M L connector, or, for a column that holds Jason or X M L text, use Parse on the Transform tab and choose Jason or X M L. Power Query shows three nested kinds. Record. What it is: One row of field and value pairs. What you do: Expand it into columns. List. What it is: An ordered series of values. What you do: To Table first, or Expand to New Rows. Table. What it is: Rows and columns. What you do: Expand the columns you need.

2.title: Convert semi-structured data to a table, continued
2.text: Convert semi-structured data to a table. The usual path is: connect, drill into the data, convert a List with To Table, expand the records into columns, expand the lists to new rows, then set the data types. Expand to New Rows repeats the parent row for every item in the list. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A list becomes a table with To Table, a record is expanded into columns, and a list column is expanded to new rows. Parse turns Jason or X M L text in a column into records.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A source file stores dates as day, month, year, and Power B I Desktop in the U S culture turns some of them into errors. What should the analyst use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Use Change Type with a day-first locale. Change Type with Locale reads the dates in the format of the culture you choose.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. An analyst needs a Size column that shows Large when Amount is at least one thousand and Small otherwise, and cannot write code. Which feature should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Conditional Column on the Amount column. Conditional Column builds if-then-else rules in a dialog without any code.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A table has one row per order line. The analyst needs one row per store with the total Amount and the number of rows. Which transformation fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Group By on Store with Sum and Count. Group By on Store with Sum of Amount and Count Rows returns one row per store.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A worksheet has one column per week of sales, and a new week column is added every Monday. The model needs one Week column and one Amount column. Which choice keeps the query working at each refresh? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Unpivot Other Columns, keeping Product. Unpivot Other Columns unpivots every column except Product, so new week columns are included.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A table lists Region, Category and Amount in rows. The analyst needs one column per Category with the sum of Amount for each Region. Which command should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Pivot Column on Category, summing Amount. Pivot Column turns the Category values into column headers and applies the Sum aggregate.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A Jason file loads in the Power Query Editor as a list of records. What should the analyst do next to get rows and columns? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Convert it to a table, then expand it. To Table turns the list into rows, and expanding the record column creates the columns.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which command turns the values of one column into new column headers? Answer: Pivot Column. Question two. Which unpivot command also unpivots columns added to the source later? Answer: Unpivot Other Columns. Question three. Which Group By operation returns a nested table of the group's rows? Answer: All Rows.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What must you do after Transpose to get headers back? Answer: Use First Row as Headers, and set the data types again. Question five. Which option reads dates in another culture's format? Answer: Change Type, Using Locale. Question six. What do you use to turn a list column into new rows? Answer: Expand to New Rows.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Data types: affect aggregation, sorting, relationships and compression; Fixed decimal number for money. New columns: Custom Column (M), Column From Examples, Conditional Column (no code), Index Column. Split and merge: Split by delimiter, characters or positions; Merge Columns with a separator; Extract. Group By: Sum, Average, Median, Min, Max, Count Rows, Count Distinct Rows, All Rows (nested table). Pivot: values become headers; needs an aggregate function. Unpivot: Unpivot Other Columns includes later columns; Only Selected Columns does not. Transpose: rows and columns swap; then Use First Row as Headers and reset types. Semi-structured: Parse for Jason or X M L; To Table for a list; expand records and lists. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
